title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming parity across Python/TS/Go, ergonomics fixes, version bump v1.15.0
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: unifying auth + retry semantics and streaming ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Over time small differences in behavior (default retry backoff, token refresh edge cases, streaming iterator APIs) have caused production inconsistencies and developer confusion. This PR consolidates shared logic, brings streaming APIs closer to parity, includes ergonomic improvements (async generators in Python, readable stream helpers in TS, context-friendly Go APIs), and bumps SDK packages to v1.15.0.

Scope and checklist: - Consolidate auth token refresh + retry wrapper into a shared internal package used by all SDKs. - Align default retry/backoff parameters and make them configurable via client options. - Stabilize streaming API surface: Python async iterator -> yields chunk objects with metadata; TS adds createReadableStream helper and consistent error events; Go adds Context-aware stream client + Close semantics. - Parity fixes: ensure identical error codes and structured error shapes across languages. - Add integration tests exercising token refresh during streaming and forced transient errors. - Bump package versions: python: 1.15.0, typescript: 1.15.0, go: v1.15.0. - Update changelogs and migration notes. - Ensure CI passes on all runtimes.

This description intentionally remains a single continuous string (sections separated by newlines).

Commit summary:
- feat(sdk-common): introduce shared auth-retry module and options mapping
- feat(python): use shared auth module; add async streaming iterator ergonomics
- feat(typescript): add createReadableStream wrapper, align retry defaults
- feat(go): add context-aware StreamClient, unify error types
- fix(tests): add flaky streaming tests and CI matrix update
- docs: update migration guide and changelogs

Files changed (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/client.py (use shared auth + new streaming iterator)
- sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py (new iterator wrapper)
- sdk/python/setup.cfg, pyproject.toml (version bump)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream.ts (createReadableStream helper)
- sdk/typescript/package.json (version bump)
- sdk/go/client/stream.go (Context-aware streaming)
- sdk/go/go.mod (version bump)
- internal/sdks/auth_retry (new shared package, adapters for each language binding)
- tests/integration/streaming_token_refresh.test (new)
- docs/sdks/migration-auth-retries.md, CHANGELOG.md

Notes on implementation: Most heavy lifting lives in internal/sdks/auth_retry, which provides token-refresh hooks, jittered exponential backoff, and a language-agnostic spec implemented with thin adapters in each language. Python now exposes an async iterator that yields {chunk, partial, meta} objects and raises structured SDKError on terminal failures. TS exposes a readable stream helper that converts the wire stream into a WHATWG Readable (and a simple async iterator wrapper). Go adds stream cancellation and explicit Close semantics to avoid goroutine leaks in long-running streams.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the shared retry logic and integration tests that spin up a local stub server to simulate transient 401/503 during streaming. CI matrix updated to include py3.11, node16/node18, go1.20. Initial run showed a flaky test on TS streaming when backpressure delay hit an edge case; fixed by introducing a short buffer and a fallback path for stream rehydration. Final CI status: all checks passed after the fix.

Migration guidance for customers (short): Most users won't need to change code. Breaking changes are limited: streaming semantics are more structured (chunks include metadata) and some error types are now normalized; see docs/sdks/migration-auth-retries.md for examples and a 5-minute migration snippet.
